_comment: Managed-settings FLOOR for the fence class. Drop into managed-settings.json (system dir), an MDM policy, or the claude.ai console — never a user/project file, which cannot lock these. Every key below was verified on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference (read 2026-09-12; the page carries no visible revision date — the server's Last-Modified was Sat, 12 Sep 2026 07:49 GMT). `permissions.deny`: 'List the tool uses Claude Code blocks' — array of permission rule strings, scope Any file. `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode`: 'Prevent anyone from entering bypassPermissions mode … rejects the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag' — type: the string "disable"; it lives UNDER permissions, not at the top level. `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`: 'Make managed settings the only settings source of permission rules' — boolean, scope Managed; with it on, allow/ask/deny rules in user, project, local and --settings files are ignored, so every allow rule an operator needs must also live here. WHAT THIS IS NOT: the same page says 'A Bash deny rule matches the command as Claude writes it, so Bash(curl *) doesn't stop /usr/bin/curl or sh -c curl …' — these rules stop the invocation Claude usually produces and are not a security boundary around the program; the PreToolUse guards in hooks/ (fence-guard sees through sh -c, eval, $(), wrappers and paths) are the second layer, and sandboxing is the third. Deny rules apply when ANY subcommand matches, including past a leading VAR=value assignment and inside $() or a for-loop body (permissions page, read the same day).
